## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
One project-policy defect should be fixed: the new `--exclude` flag does not take its default from an `ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE` environment variable, so CI cannot set exclusions through the environment the way the flag reference requires.

## Changes
The pull request adds a repeatable `--exclude GLOB` option to `cli/main.py`. `collect()` uses it to skip files whose base name matches any pattern, and logs each skip. It also documents the flag in `docs/flags.md`, adds parser, collection and end-to-end archive tests in `tests/test_main.py`, and adds the fixture `tests/fixtures/hostile-review.txt`.

## Critical
(none)

## Important
- cli/main.py:17 — correctness — Read the --exclude default from ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE — When CI sets `ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE=*.log`, the run still archives `.log` files, because the flag uses a hard-coded `default=[]` and never reads the environment. This breaks the rule "Every command-line flag added under `cli/` from now on must also take its default from an `ARCHIVE_<NAME>` environment variable" (.agents/skills/cli-flags/reference.md:5). — CI pipelines that set options through the environment cannot exclude files, so unwanted files end up in their archives. — Fix: Build the default from `os.environ.get("ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE")` with a documented separator for multiple globs, note the variable in `docs/flags.md:7`, and extend `test_exclude_defaults_to_nothing` with a monkeypatched-environment case.
